newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Normandy Q2 gold output up 9.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Normandy Q2 gold output up 9.1 pct.

text.p: Normandy Mining Ltd said on Thursday its gold production for the December quarter was up 9.1 percent from the September quarter at 378,117 ounces, at a total cash cost of A$337 an ounce, down from A$360.

In its quarterly report, Normandy said total attributable gold production rose to 36 percent to 341,300 ounces from 250,525 as a result of the merger with Gold Mines of Kalgoorlie Ltd and Posgold Ltd, excluding La Source operations.

After adjusting for disposed operations, Jubilee and Bounty, direct gold production of 250,221 ounces was 65 percent higher than the 151,821 ounces reported by Posgold in the previous quarter, Normandy said.

Normandy said it had continued to improve its asset portfolio with Mine Or's increased stake in the Ity mine in Cote d'Ivoire, the sale of its Bounty mine stake, and mine development at Callie (Northern Territory), Ovacik (Turkey) and Vera-Nancy (Queensland).

"These portfolio changes, together with the sale of Jubilee in May 1996, will impact positively on the company's production performance and long-term profitability," executive chairman Robert Champion de Crespigny said.
De Crespigny said Normandy had adopted the North American Gold Institute standard for reporting gold production costs on a per ounce basis.
The Normandy group had hedged a total 4.628 million ounces at an average A$740 an ounce to the yaer 2006, the report said.
